items.t: Authorize $500,000 for Cincinnati USA Convention & Visitors Bureau operational support

items.sm: Establishes the "Hazard Pay" American Rescue Plan project account and appropriates $2,800,000 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund to give employees additional compensation during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $500,000 for the Place Based Investigations of Violent Offender Territories program in the Cincinnati Police Department during the fiscal year 2022 budget.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $430,375 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund to upgrade and expand the City's cybersecurity program during the fiscal year 2022 budget.

items.t: Appropriate $250,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for Sawyer Point tennis courts

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $1,000,000 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund for operational support to the Main Street Ventures Partnership with the City.

items.sm: Establishes the HARBOR project account, and transfers and appropriates $500,000 from the HOME-American Rescue Plan account to the Department of Buildings and Inspections for the Homeowner Assistance Repairs and Building Order Remission Program.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $100,000 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund to expand the ShotSpotter program in the Cincinnati Police Department during the fiscal year 2022 budget.

items.t: Appropriate $3,000,000 for the Cincinnati USA Convention & Visitors Bureau
items.sm: Establishes an American Rescue Plan project account and appropriates $3,000,000 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund for operational support to the Cincinnati USA Convention & Visitors Bureau.

items.t: Appropriate $3,000,000 for the Warsaw Creative Campus in East Price Hill
items.sm: Establishes an American Rescue Plan project account and appropriates $3,000,000 to Price Hill Will for the Warsaw Creative Campus project in East Price Hill.

items.sm: Establishes an American Rescue Plan project account and appropriates $60,000 to The Salvation Army of Southwest Ohio and Northeast Kentucky for its Anti-Human Trafficking Program and End Slavery Cincinnati program.

items.t: Appropriate $50,000 for Grant Us Hope teen suicide prevention
items.sm: Establishes an American Rescue Plan project account and appropriates $50,000 to the nonprofit Grant Us Hope to further its mission of teen suicide prevention.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $2,900,000 to Cincinnati Children's Hospital to expand its College Hill campus to address the behavioral health needs of children.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $1,000,000 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund to preserve the First Lutheran Church Tower in Over-the-Rhine.

items.sm: Establishes a grant project account and appropriates $5,558,964 from the Local Fiscal Recovery Fund for a Neighborhood Childcare Relief Fund supporting child care initiatives and programs.

items.t: Ask the Administration to include American Rescue Plan funds for the Western Hills Viaduct
items.sm: Asks the Administration to include enough anticipated American Rescue Plan funds in the fiscal year 2022 budget to meet remaining Western Hills Viaduct construction funding needs.

items.t: Use American Rescue Plan funds for police recruits, mental health response and youth programs
items.sm: Asks Council to commit part of the American Rescue Plan appropriation to a 2021 police recruit class, Mental Health Response Team training and youth and victim assistance programs.

items.sm: Asks the Administration to budget $1,400,000 for an additional class of 43 police recruits, funded first by a COPS Hiring grant and then the American Rescue Plan.

items.t: Use American Rescue Plan Act funds for reserves and budget deficits
items.sm: Asks Council to use the first American Rescue Plan Act funds to reach the 16.7% reserve target, close fiscal year 2022 and 2023 deficits, and make whole other City funds hurt by COVID-19.

items.t: Allocate American Rescue Plan Act funds to address City staffing shortages
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate American Rescue Plan Act funds to address staffing shortages identified by department heads and recommended by the Administration.

items.t: Request American Rescue Plan Act funds for renovating the Evanston Field House
items.sm: Asks that American Rescue Plan Act funds be allocated to renovate the Evanston Field House, which is estimated to cost $275,000 to $396,000.

items.t: Ask for American Rescue Plan Act funds for a new District 5 police headquarters
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate an estimated $20 million to $25 million in American Rescue Plan Act funds to build a new Cincinnati Police District 5 headquarters.

items.t: Allocate $100,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funds to the Neighborhood Street Calming Program
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $100,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to fund the Department of Transportation and Engineering's Neighborhood Street Calming Program for speed humps in 2022.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $350,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to The Mark, a nonprofit, to help stabilize and purchase St. Mark Church at 3500 Montgomery Rd. in Evanston.

items.sm: Asks Council to fund the HARBOR program with $2 million from the American Rescue Plan Act to help low- and moderate-income homeowners with housing code violations, with possible loans for higher earners.

items.sm: Asks Council to deposit $50 million into the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and have community councils annually consider transferring portions of Tax Increment Financing and Voluntary Tax Incentive Contribution Agreement affordable housing funds.

items.sm: Asks the Administration to draft an ordinance giving $3,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to the Cincinnati USA Convention & Visitor Bureau to restore staffing and recover from pandemic losses.

items.t: Allocate American Rescue Plan Act funds to three neighborhood projects
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate American Rescue Plan Act funds, in amounts to be determined, to Camp Washington road improvements, the Taft/McMillan Two-Way project and the OTR Bell Tower restoration.

items.t: Draft an ordinance providing $60,000 for anti-human trafficking outreach
items.sm: Asks the Administration to draft an ordinance providing $60,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to The Salvation Army's Anti-Human Trafficking Program and End Slavery Cincinnati for outreach to human trafficking victims.

items.t: Commit American Rescue Plan funds to the Wesley Chapel Mission Center
items.sm: Asks Council to commit a portion of the City's American Rescue Plan appropriation to the Wesley Chapel Mission Center for its programs and building site improvements.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $1 million in American Rescue Plan Act funds to return the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. statue to Reading Road and Martin Luther King Drive.

items.t: Consider the motion and documents presented to the Human Services Chamber
items.sm: Asks Council to consider the attached motion and supporting documents that were presented to the Human Services Chamber.

items.t: Allocate American Rescue Plan Act funds to Flywheel Social Enterprise
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate up to $300,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funds to Flywheel Social Enterprise to expand equity-focused programs and support at least 20 diverse startup founders.

items.t: Consider $50,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for Co-op Cincy's Business Legacy program
items.sm: Asks Council to consider Co-op Cincy's request for $50,000 from the American Rescue Plan for a revolving loan funding technical assistance for businesses exploring transition to worker ownership.

items.t: Allocate $450,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funds for Contemporary Arts Center bathrooms
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $450,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to create accessible and inclusive bathroom facilities at the Cincinnati Contemporary Arts Center.

items.t: Allocate $2.8 million to UC Health for the Emergency Medical Services Canopy
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $2.8 million in American Rescue Plan Act funds to UC Health to complete the Emergency Medical Services Canopy on Goodman Street.

items.t: Grant American Rescue Plan Act funds to the Cincinnati Music Festival
items.sm: Asks Council to grant $100,000 for the 2021 virtual Cincinnati Music Festival and $250,000 for the 2022 live event from American Rescue Plan Act funding.

items.t: Allocate $150,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to the All-In Cincinnati initiative
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $150,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to the Greater Cincinnati Foundation's All-In Cincinnati for COVID-19 community engagement and inclusive prosperity for Black women.

items.t: Allocate $1,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to expand the Youth2Work program
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $1,000,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to expand the Cincinnati Recreation Commission's Youth2Work program to serve at least 1,000 youth ages 14 to 24.

items.t: Allocate $5,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for the Collaborative Agreement Refresh
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $5,000,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to fully enact the Collaborative Agreement Refresh, focusing on reform, accountability, case investigations and data analysis.

items.t: Allocate $15,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to the I Hear Music Gospel Fest
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $15,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to I Hear Music, Inc. for the annual I Hear Music Gospel Fest.

items.t: Allocate $50,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to expand the Community Court
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $50,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to expand the Community Court, an unofficial juvenile court, to help youth stay out of the court and prison system.

items.t: Allocate $154,055 in American Rescue Plan funds to Keep Cincinnati Beautiful
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $154,055 from the American Rescue Plan Act to Keep Cincinnati Beautiful's Environmental Services Program to deter and prevent illegal dumping.

items.t: Allocate $1,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for the Pendleton Heritage Center renovation
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $1,000,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to complete the renovation of the Pendleton Heritage Center in the East End.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $40,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to the Avondale Development Corporation for the Avondale Fence Art Project and its Youth Ambassadors Program.

items.t: Allocate $8,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for the Robert O'Neal Multicultural Arts Center
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $8,000,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to close the funding gap for the Robert O'Neal Multicultural Arts Center in the West End.

items.t: Allocate $25,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to the Midwest Regional Black Family Reunion
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $25,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to the Midwest Regional Black Family Reunion, managed by I Hear Music, Inc.

items.t: Allocate $150,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funds to the Bond Hill Community Council
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $150,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to the Bond Hill Community Council to fund a Community Organizer and a needs assessment.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $1.5 million from the American Rescue Plan Act for a Cincinnati Childcare Relief Fund, managed by 4C for Children, to eliminate delinquent payments owed to licensed childcare facilities.

items.t: Allocate $300,000 in American Rescue Plan Act funds to the Boys and Girls Club for tutoring
items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $300,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to the Boys and Girls Club of America, Cincinnati Branch, for tutoring.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $500,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to The Center for Closing the Health Gap to purchase its own facility.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $200,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to Seven Hills Neighborhood Houses for operational support of its Victims of Crime Advocate and Trauma Recovery Center.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $10,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to each of 51 community councils, totaling $510,000, to offset revenue lost to COVID-related cancellations.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $100,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to Professional Artistic Research to help finalize acquisition of 15,000 square feet of industrial mixed-use property in Northside.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $3,000,000 from the American Rescue Plan Act to MORTAR, with $2,500,000 for the MORTAR Mall and $500,000 for an online learning platform.

items.sm: Asks the Administration to draft an ordinance establishing an Emergency Relief Fund, using American Rescue Plan funding, for time-sensitive aid to pandemic-affected small businesses and nonprofits.

items.sm: Asks Council to adopt a framework that prioritizes City fiscal stability, then emergency relief for jobs and housing, then transformative and capital investments, for distributing American Rescue Plan funding.

items.sm: Asks Council to allocate $250,000 in anticipated American Rescue Plan funds to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Cincinnati to expand programs addressing pandemic learning loss.

items.sm: Asks the City to allocate $900,000 to Cintrifuse for its plan for green-skilling and startup-skilling in the urban Over-the-Rhine core.

items.sm: Asks that $600,000 of American Rescue Plan funds go to La Soupe ($250,000), Last Mile Food Rescue ($100,000) and Produce Perks ($250,000).

items.t: Authorize acceptance of $29,906 from the Ohio TechCred Credential Reimbursement Program
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for and accept up to $29,906 for Cincinnati Police Department employees' technology-focused credentials and to appropriate the funds to the Department's non-personnel operating budget.

items.t: Amend Ordinance No. 0166-2021 to revise an American Rescue Plan account description
items.sm: Amends Ordinance No. 0166-2021 to remove "Summer" from the description of American Rescue Plan account ARP065, "Cincinnati Recreation Commission Extended Hours."

items.t: Approve a tax exemption agreement with The Farmers Hotel, LLC for 4000 and 4004 Colerain Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with The Farmers Hotel, LLC for a 12-year, 100% exemption on a roughly $645,000 remodeling in Northside.

items.t: Authorize General Fund transfers of $700,000 and $1,152,123 for City department needs
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $700,000 from the Reserve for Weather Related Events, Other Emergency and One-Time Needs to the General Fund surplus and transferring $1,152,123 within the General Fund to realign department funding.

items.t: Authorize $1,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds for hazard pay for City employees
items.sm: Authorizes transferring and appropriating $1,000,000 in American Rescue Plan funds and one-time hazard pay payments to qualifying represented and non-represented City employees, excluding the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees bargaining unit.

items.t: Authorize $1 million in capital funding for Findlay Market improvements and renovations
items.sm: Establishes two capital project accounts and transfers and appropriates $500,000 from each of two funds for permanent improvements and renovations at City-owned Findlay Market, declaring the expenditures a public purpose.

items.t: Authorize capital project account changes and transfers for the Capital Improvement Program
items.sm: Authorizes establishing 9 new capital project accounts and transferring and appropriating funds among capital and operating accounts, including $65,000 for Center Hill Landfill systems and $54,000 for a Town Center Garage study.

items.t: Authorize a driveway encroachment easement for HTS Properties LLC on Bercliff Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Grant of Easement giving HTS Properties LLC a driveway encroachment easement on Bercliff Avenue in Northside.

items.t: Authorize a property sale agreement with 7AD Properties, LTD. for portions of three avenues
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Property Sale Agreement with 7AD Properties, LTD. to vacate and convey portions of Creston, Coney and East Epworth Avenues in Spring Grove Village.

items.t: Establish accounts and accept a grant for Harrison and Kling Avenue traffic calming
items.sm: Establishes two project accounts, accepts up to $225,000 from the Ohio Department of Transportation and appropriates $75,000 from Westwood 1 Equivalent Fund 496 for traffic calming at Harrison Avenue and Kling Avenue.

items.t: Authorize encroachment easements for CLC Main Street LLC on Third and Main Streets
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Grant of Easement giving CLC Main Street LLC encroachment easements on portions of Third and Main Streets in the Central Business District.

items.t: Approve a property sale agreement with TSMT, LLC for 218 Mulberry Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Property Sale and Development Agreement with TSMT, LLC to sell City-owned property at 218 Mulberry Street in Mt. Auburn for about 10 residential units.

items.t: Express support for the current design of the Gateway to Freedom Park
items.sm: Expresses the support of the Mayor and Council for the current design of the Gateway to Freedom Park, to be built on Lot 18 at the Banks.

items.t: Amend the Uptown SEQ Holdings property sale agreement in Avondale
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to amend the agreement with Uptown SEQ Holdings, LLC to extend the developer's option to purchase City-controlled property at Martin Luther King Drive and Reading Road.

items.t: Authorize a Property Sale and Development Agreement for 120 W. Elder Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute an agreement with TI PM, LLC for the sale of the upper levels of the City-owned building at 120 W. Elder Street for residential redevelopment.

items.t: Authorize a Lease and Management Agreement with the Corporation for Findlay Market of Cincinnati
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute an agreement under which the Corporation for Findlay Market of Cincinnati leases and manages property near Findlay Market for up to 10 years.

items.t: Approve a tax exemption agreement with 726 E McMillan LLC
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Community Reinvestment Area agreement giving a 12-year, 100% tax exemption for remodeling 726 E. McMillan Street into 10 residential units and commercial space.

items.t: Authorize a Property Sale and Development Agreement for 2859 Fischer Place
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute an agreement with Randall Walton and Trina Walton for the sale of City-owned property at 2859 Fischer Place in Westwood.

items.t: Express support for accommodating the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Cincinnati
items.sm: Expresses the Mayor's and Council's intent to modify laws and policies and to issue permits, concessions and licenses promptly to accommodate FIFA and its partners for 2026 World Cup matches and events in Cincinnati.

items.t: Exempt FIFA from admissions tax for 2026 World Cup matches
items.sm: Authorizes, notwithstanding Cincinnati Municipal Code Chapter 309, an exemption for FIFA and its subsidiaries from collecting and remitting admissions tax on 2026 World Cup matches in Cincinnati.

items.t: Authorize an aerial encroachment easement for Textile Partners, LLC
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to grant Textile Partners, LLC an aerial encroachment easement above portions of Elm, West Fourth and McFarland Streets in the Central Business District.

items.t: Approve the Sayler Park Plan as the planning guide for the neighborhood
items.sm: Approves the Sayler Park Plan as the planning guide for the Sayler Park neighborhood.

items.t: Report on code changes for private curbside electric vehicle charging stations
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's response to Councilmember Mann's motion assessing the code changes needed to allow privately owned curbside charging stations next to properties with electric vehicles.

items.t: Designate St. Mark's Church Building in Evanston as a local historic landmark
items.sm: Designates the St. Mark's Church Building at 3500 Montgomery Road in the Evanston neighborhood as a local historic landmark.

items.t: Rezone properties in Mount Auburn from Park and Recreation to Office General
items.sm: Amends the official zoning map to rezone 2429 Macaulay Street, 2434 Vine Street and 13 E. McMillan Street from Park and Recreation to Office General to allow residential redevelopment.

items.t: Authorize revocable street privileges for minor right-of-way uses

items.t: Authorize artwork on the stairway between Van Leer Street and Ohio Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to design, install and maintain artwork on the CUF stairway between Van Leer Street and Ohio Avenue, notwithstanding conflicting regulations or Municipal Code provisions.

items.t: Clarify the summer and winter water rate months for political subdivisions
items.sm: Modifies Section 401-81, "Charges to Political Subdivisions," of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to clarify the months when the summer and winter rates apply to political subdivisions.

items.t: Modify the salary range schedule for the City Planning Director
items.sm: Amends Section 490, Division 5, of Chapter 307 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to establish a new salary range schedule for the City Planning Director classification.

items.t: Establish regulations for e-scooter rental franchises
items.sm: Creates Chapter 811, "e-Scooter Rental Franchises," in the Cincinnati Municipal Code and amends Section 1501-9, "Class D Civil Offenses," to establish e-scooters in the City.

items.t: Establish e-scooter rental franchises in the City
items.sm: Establishes e-scooter rental franchises in Cincinnati by creating Chapter 811 of the Municipal Code and amending Section 1507-9, "Class D Civil Offenses."

items.sm: Asks the Administration to conduct a parking study for the Madison and Whetsel Business District, funded with $30,000 from the Madisonville District TIF and shared with community stakeholders.

items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on the Smart Cities Platform, referencing document #202100599.

items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on additional stop signs at Middleton and Lafayette, Hanfield and Gordon, Pitts and Chase, Teakwood and Devonwood, Mad Anthony and Knowlton, and Pullan and Langland.

items.t: Report on Erie Avenue and Cincinnati Police Department District 2 pedestrian safety
items.sm: Submits the City Manager's report on pedestrian safety on Erie Avenue and in Cincinnati Police Department District 2.

items.t: Legislative Agent Registration for Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center
items.sm: Registration of legislative agent from Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center for government relations activities.

items.t: Report on the Smart Cities Platform
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on the Smart Cities Platform, referencing document #202100599.

items.t: Remove the obsolete workhouse confinement penalty for emergency order violations
items.sm: Amends Article XVIII, Section 11 of the Administrative Code to remove the obsolete "confinement in the workhouse" penalty for violating orders issued during a state of emergency.

items.t: Dedicate property as public right-of-way for East McMillan Street and Auburn Avenue
items.sm: Dedicates, accepts and confirms certain real property as public right-of-way for portions of East McMillan Street and Auburn Avenue in the Mt. Auburn neighborhood.

items.t: Accept in-kind donations from the Cincinnati Parks Foundation
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept park supplies, professional services and contracted services valued at approximately $8,632 from the Cincinnati Parks Foundation to improve various City parks.

items.t: Accept a $150,000 grant to integrate oral health care with primary care
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $150,000 from the HealthPath Foundation of Ohio and deposit it into Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Establish the Golf Course Improvements project and transfer $800,000
items.sm: Establishes capital project account no. 980x195x221907 and transfers $800,000 from Municipal Golf Activities Fund 105 for the Reeves Driving Range reconstruction, pavement repairs and other improvements.

items.t: Apply for a $250,000 grant for the Live-Work-Play Cincinnati program
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $250,000 from the Get Cincy Fed Buyers Club Initiative Grant and deposit it into Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Transfer $375,554.94 for incoming Councilmembers' operating budgets
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $375,554.94 within the General Fund among City Council operating budget accounts to provide resources for incoming Councilmembers for the remainder of fiscal year 2022.

items.t: Accept a utility easement from Grand Communities, LLC for watermains
items.sm: Accepts and confirms a permanent utility easement from Grand Communities, LLC for watermains in the Magnolia Woods Subdivision, Section 3 in Colerain Township.

items.t: Authorize a $4,590 payment to US Bank for HOME Administration expenses
items.sm: Authorizes a $4,590 payment from the HOME Administration '19 project account to US Bank as a moral obligation for purchase card expenses.

items.t: Establish the Madisonville Business District Public Parking TIF project and appropriate $460,000
items.sm: Establishes a capital project account and transfers $430,000 to it, plus $30,000 to the Department of Community and Economic Development, from the Madisonville District Equivalent Fund 498 to improve public parking.

items.t: Establish the Recreation Improvements project and appropriate $1,500,000
items.sm: Establishes the Recreation Improvements capital project account and appropriates $1,500,000 from the Recreation Special Activities Fund 323 for renovations, security cameras and signage at recreation centers and outdoor areas.

items.t: Accept and appropriate a $150,000 State grant for recreation improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate a $150,000 Ohio Department of Natural Resources grant for improvements at Findlay Playground, Grant Park and the Over-the-Rhine Recreation Center.

items.t: Authorize a $5,099 payment to US Bank for Cincinnati Recreation Commission training charges
items.sm: Authorizes a $5,099 payment to US Bank as a moral obligation for trainings and conferences billed as one purchase card transaction exceeding the State's $3,000 limit.

items.t: Accept the transfer of Homeland Security grants for the Greater Cincinnati Fusion Center
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $548,048.39 in four Homeland Security grants from the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office, making the Cincinnati Police Department the lead agency for the Greater Cincinnati Fusion Center.

items.t: Authorize transfers of Neighborhood Stabilization funds for projects in Northside
items.sm: Authorizes returning $152,303.30 to Fund 438 and appropriating $355,552.78 from its surplus for Neighborhood Stabilization Program 1 and 3 target areas in Northside.

items.t: Authorize a $3,112 transfer to realign City Councilmember office budgets
items.sm: Authorizes the transfer of $3,112 within the General Fund among operating budget accounts to realign the office budgets of various City Councilmembers.

items.t: Authorize the acceptance of donations from Indigo Sports for youth Christmas activities
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept a $2,585 donation and in-kind gifts to support the Cincinnati Recreation Commission's youth Christmas activities, and deposits the money into Fund 319.

items.t: Authorize a $177,000 transfer for COVID-19 homeless shelter improvements
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $177,000 within the General Fund and accepting up to $177,000 from Hamilton County's Coronavirus Relief Fund for COVID-19 related homeless shelter improvements.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a $1,000 grant for youth sports programs
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a grant of up to $1,000 from the Cincinnati Recreation Foundation to support youth sports programs in need.

items.t: Authorize utility-funded replacement of private lead service lines
items.sm: Authorizes Greater Cincinnati Water Works to provide 100% utility-funded private lead service line replacement, subject to available funds, when the property owner and the City have a contract.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a $150,000 donation for the Corryville Recreation Center
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept an in-kind donation from Uptown Rental Properties valued at $150,000 for fitness equipment, scoreboards and other improvements at the Corryville Recreation Center.

items.t: Approve a 15-year tax exemption agreement for development in the West End
items.sm: Approves a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Seven Hills Neighborhood Houses and the Port of Greater Cincinnati Development Authority for remodeling 3 buildings into 16 rental units and commercial space.

items.t: Approve a 15-year tax exemption agreement for development on Warsaw Avenue
items.sm: Approves a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with Warsaw Creative LLC and the Port of Greater Cincinnati Development Authority for remodeling 7 buildings at 3108-3120 Warsaw Avenue into 13 rental units and commercial space.

items.t: Approve a 12-year tax exemption agreement for 2001 Vine Street
items.sm: Approves a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with 2001 Vine, LLC for remodeling a building at 2001 Vine Street into 4 rental units and commercial space.

items.t: Approve a 12-year tax exemption agreement for 1209 Elm Street
items.sm: Approves a Community Reinvestment Area Tax Exemption Agreement with 1209 Elm, LLC for remodeling a building at 1209 Elm Street into 4 residential rental units.

items.t: Authorize a property sale agreement for 127 Green Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Property Sale and Development Agreement with The Acanthus Group, LLC for the sale of City-owned property at 127 Green Street in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Classify improvements at 3035 Clifton Avenue for a residential tax abatement
items.sm: Classifies improvements at 3035 Clifton Avenue in CUF as residential improvements eligible for a real property tax abatement, notwithstanding Ordinance Nos. 274-2017, 275-2017, 276-2017 and 370-2020.

items.t: Authorize a property sale for apartments and townhomes in Mt. Auburn
items.sm: Authorizes a Property Sale and Development Agreement with Auburn Land Holdings LLC for City property in Mt. Auburn, to build 270 market-rate apartments and 5 townhomes.

items.t: Request a parking study for the Madison and Whetsel Business District
items.sm: Asks the Administration to conduct a parking study for the Madison and Whetsel Business District, funded with $30,000 from the Madisonville District TIF and shared with community stakeholders.

items.t: Authorize lease and development agreements for the Lunken Airport Terminal Building
items.sm: Authorizes a lease of up to 50 years, a development agreement and a service agreement with vR Hospitality LLC for redeveloping the Lunken Airport Terminal Building, with a rebate of service payments in lieu of taxes.

items.t: Declare a 30-year tax exemption for Lunken Airport Terminal Building improvements
items.sm: Declares improvements at 262 Wilmer Avenue, including the Lunken Airport Terminal Building, a public purpose and exempts them from real property taxation for 30 years under Ohio Revised Code Section 5709.41.

items.t: Authorize a lease of Lunken Airport property for a fixed-base operator business
items.sm: Authorizes the City to lease Lease Area 52 at Lunken Airport to vR Hospitality LLC for up to 40 years for aircraft fuel sales, storage and servicing.

items.t: Report on pedestrian safety for Roll Hill School students
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's December 13, 2021 report on pedestrian safety for Roll Hill School students.

items.t: Establish and fund a $500,000 Red Bike Program Expansion project
items.sm: Establishes a capital project and transfers and appropriates $500,000 from the General Fund to expand the Red Bike program to Bond Hill, Roselawn, Evanston and Avondale.

items.t: Approve the creation of the Westwood DORA outdoor refreshment area
items.sm: Approves an application to create the Westwood DORA, a designated outdoor refreshment area in Westwood under Chapter 838, and authorizes the City Manager to take necessary actions for its operation and maintenance.
